title: Testing Fundamentals in TypeScript: Edge Cases, Test Doubles, Flaky Tests & Mutants
concept: Write tests that find bugs instead of confirming happy paths: choose the cheapest test that catches the bug, cover boundaries and invalid input, control time and shared state, use fakes where they help, fix flaky tests, and measure your tests by the mutants they kill.
description: A beginner course for developers who write tests because CI asks for them and want the tests to start catching bugs. Every lesson starts from a situation on the CodeDev learning platform - a certificate refused at exactly 80% because of an off-by-one, a deadline test that failed every night at midnight, a service test that needed a real database, a pipeline that went red one run in five, a test suite that stayed green when the pricing rule was deleted - and fixes it with a habit you can check: unit, integration or end-to-end, boundaries and invalid input, assertions that fail for the right reason, an injected clock, fakes and mocks at the right boundary, isolation, the Fix the Flaky Pipeline scenario, an AI-written edge-case bug, writing tests that are graded by the mutants they kill, and mutation testing. 10 lessons with True/False quizzes on real tests and logs, and TypeScript challenges graded by hidden tests.

learningOutcomes.text: Choose unit, integration or end-to-end tests and write assertions that fail for the right reason
Cover happy paths, boundaries, invalid input and repeated requests
Control time, randomness and shared state so tests are deterministic and isolated
Use fakes, stubs and mocks at the right boundary instead of mocking everything
Recognise flaky tests and tests that cannot fail, and measure tests with mutants

knownIssues: No test framework in the code runner: in lesson 3.3 learners write test cases as data that a small runner executes against the correct code and planted mutants
